device.name: Lutron Caseta Smart Bridge 2
device.notes: Lutron Caseta Smart Bridge 2 advertises multiple local services. LEAP on port 8081 is the modern local TLS JSON/WebSocket control protocol. LAP on port 8083 is deprecated. The _lutron._tcp status service exposes stable bridge identity including MACADDR, firmware CODEVER, system type, and device class. HomeKit HAP is separately advertised on port 4548.

issued_to_client: Client certificate and private key signed by the bridge CA
credentials.notes: This is the strongest local auth model of any device documented here: no shared secret, no cloud, and a client credential that can be revoked by resetting the bridge.

factory_reset.effect: Network reset only: drops network settings and external integrations (including issued client certificates). Per Lutron documentation this does NOT delete previously paired devices, scenes or schedules; no button procedure wipes the associated-device list.

procedures.indicator: Release the button once the light ring begins to blink.
procedures.name: Rear button held 20s (network reset)

steps.action: Press and hold the small black button on the back of the bridge for 20 seconds; release when the light ring begins to blink.
steps.notes: Vendor-documented network reset; paired devices, scenes and schedules survive. A 40-second hold (LED flashes again at 40s) performs a HomeKit reset.

methods.description: Ethernet to the router; the bridge takes a DHCP lease and advertises _lutron._tcp.local.

steps.action: Connect the bridge with Ethernet and apply power.

methods.description: The client generates a key pair and CSR, then presents it while the physical button on the back of the bridge is held. The bridge signs the CSR and returns the client certificate plus its own CA certificate, which the client pins for all later LEAP sessions.

steps.action: Generate an RSA/EC key pair and a certificate signing request on the client.
Press and hold the button on the back of the bridge.
Submit the CSR to the bridge's pairing service and store the signed certificate, private key and bridge CA.
steps.expect: Signed client certificate returned; later LEAP connections on port 8081 authenticate with it.

request.service: LAP pairing (TLS-JSON on port 8083, not HTTP)

setup.notes: The Caseta bridge is Ethernet-only, so there is no WiFi provisioning. What does need documenting is the LEAP pairing handshake, because unlike most devices here the bridge issues the client a real X.509 certificate and refuses anonymous connections afterwards.

rejoin.notes: A router change is a cable move; issued client certificates survive. Clients must rediscover the bridge by TXT MACADDR, not by IP.

http_endpoints.description: Placeholder for the LEAP TLS JSON/WebSocket service on port 8081; control uses LEAP messages rather than plain unauthenticated REST.
http_endpoints.name: LEAP Service Root
